what_this_is_not: Not an assertion-shaped boolean. L3 AC-05 reproduced that a synthetic read-back naming an all-zero commit passed the producer's own verifier, so a record claiming success proves nothing. This record is the output of fetching the branch from GitHub into an empty directory over the network and recomputing every digest there.

functional_read_back_from_the_clone.why: Digest equality proves the bytes arrived. It does not prove the bundle is internally consistent. These three commands were run inside the clone, against only the files that were published.
functional_read_back_from_the_clone.provctl_check: PASS - 86 constraints, each classified, each citation checkable

bootstrap_declared.what_it_covers: The 15 bundle files that existed at 7dbc7177, recomputed byte-identical from an independent clone.
bootstrap_declared.what_it_cannot_cover: MANIFEST.json and REMOTE-READBACK.json are written after the commit they attest and are published in the following commit. A record cannot hash the commit that contains it. The manifest closes over this record; this record attests the commit before the manifest. That circularity is declared here rather than hidden, which is the only honest handling of it.
bootstrap_declared.how_a_verifier_closes_the_loop: Fetch the final branch head, recompute every entry in MANIFEST.json, recompute bundle_sha256 over the entries array, and confirm that the files this record attests are byte-identical at the final head. Two commits, one continuous chain of digests.
